findings.reason: the §8 retention node should add one running-job query to `slurm.py` and have retention call it, rather than ship another forked scheduler query that drifts from the others on flags and failure handling.
findings.text: the retention eligibility check shells out to `squeue` itself (`default_running_job_ids`) instead of asking the package's SLURM owner `imas_ambix/agent/slurm.py`; the package already carries eight other direct `squeue` call sites in `cli.py` (1087, 1244, 1983, 2008, 2306, 2341, 3239), each re-deriving the same `-h -u <user> -A <account> -o <fmt>` query and its error handling, so the plan's "not running" rule adds a ninth copy of a mechanism the rubric names as a recurring duplicate

findings.reason: a store whose path the design owns but never places through the owner will drift from the ingest service and its readers, the same reader/writer disagreement §5 exists to remove.
findings.text: the store's path `DEFAULT_INDEX_PATH = ~/.cache/ambix/watch-index.sqlite3` is a module literal repeated verbatim in three `cli.py` help strings (2685, 2785, 2880), and §2/§5 — which define and place the persistent store — never route it through `SiteConfig`, the owner that already resolves `receipts_dir`, `price_table` and `endpoint_document` "by construction rather than by two constants agreeing" (`imas_ambix/agent/profile.py:676`); §12 does exactly this for the price table and the plan's own handoff comment lists the index path as a thin interface to cut, but no section or followup carries it

findings.reason: the supplied counts are 0/0/0/0 and both options are already deployed, so recording their accounting changes no build.
findings.text: the section adds the in-repo `watch --live` CLI option (and its `live`/`lane` JSON subset) while naming only removals that live in the dotfiles repository (`_scrape_serve`, the `/metrics` fetch), so within this repository the option is pure added surface with no retirement or merge stated; §8's `retire-raw` option is in the same position

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the modules the design adds each hide substantial behaviour behind one entry point (`provider_prices` hides fetch/atomic write/ageing; `live_panel` hides the lane copy and the single-run trailing-window derivation; `watch_publish` hides in-process derivation and the atomic rename), and §8's store change is a deepening (one `counter_run_continues` predicate shared by compactor and query) rather than a set of shallow wrappers.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §8's retention liveness check reimplements a scheduler query inside `telemetry_retention.py` rather than extending the package's SLURM owner `imas_ambix/agent/slurm.py`; and §2/§5 own the persistent store but never resolve its path through `watch.py`'s existing site-configuration owner (`imas_ambix/agent/profile.py`), so a literal is repeated across `watch.py` and `cli.py`.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §11 adds the in-repo `watch --live` CLI option with no text naming what it retires or merges, or why nothing can be (§5 accounts for `ingest` by removing the SLURM service generator and `--submit`/`--dry-run`; §10/§12 account for theirs by deleting gpu-watch's ledger, price fetch and `DEFAULT_PRICE_PATH`).
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan searched and cites what it extends: §3 names the spine's existing run rule (`counter_span`, `_prefix_hit_rate`), §8 names `partitioned_total` and `compact_rows`, §11 names the lane document and reckon's lane reader, §12 names `watch.DEFAULT_PRICE_PATH`, `SiteConfig`, `match_price`/`price_at`/`ledger_cost`, and §5 names reckon's declared-services mechanism, and the landed modules reuse `request_receipts.STATUS_COMPLETED` and `lane.classify_reading` rather than reimplementing them.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the one thin layer, `watch_publish` forwarding to `watch.watch_document`, is justified in the plan's own text: the 48 s derivation must run on the fleet allocation, not on the login node gpu-watch runs on, so a caller cannot be pointed at watch.py directly.
